questions.question: To which of the following dynasties did Queen Rudramadevi belong?
questions.solution:
Queen Rudramadevi (1262–1289) belonged to the Kakatiya Dynasty of Warangal.
  • She was one of the few women to rule as a monarch in India.
  • The traveler Marco Polo visited her kingdom.

questions.question: Vikramaditya VI, whose biography was composed by his court poet Bilhana, was a ruler of ______ dynasty.
questions.solution:
Vikramaditya VI was a ruler of the Western Chalukya Dynasty.
  • His court poet Bilhana wrote his biography titled 'Vikramankadevacharita'.

questions.question: Which of the following organisations was the earliest to be established, as compared with the other three during British rule?
questions.solution:
The Brahmo Samaj (founded 1828) was the earliest among the listed reform organizations.
  • Prarthana Samaj (1867), Satya Shodhak Samaj (1873).

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of Prarthana Samaj?
questions.solution:
Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj in Bombay in 1867.
  • It was popularized by M.G. Ranade.

questions.question: Of the following sites of Harappan Civilization, which one is NOT located in Pakistan?
questions.solution:
Shortughai is a Harappan trading post located in Afghanistan.
  • Kot Diji, Chanhudaro, and Balakot are located in Pakistan.

questions.question: Of the following battles fought by Akbar, which one was the latest as compared to the rest of the battles?
questions.solution:
The Battle of Haldighati (1576) was the latest among those listed.
  • Panipat II (1556), Thanesar (1567), Tukaroi (1575).

questions.question: When was the first battle of Panipat fought?
questions.solution:
The First Battle of Panipat took place on 21 April 1526.
  • It introduced gunpowder and artillery to Indian warfare.

questions.question: Which of the following Vedas dealt with music?
questions.solution:
The Sama Veda is the Veda of Melodies and Chants.
  • It is considered the root of Indian classical music.

questions.question: Which dynasty ruled India between 320 AD and 550 AD?
questions.solution:
The Gupta Dynasty ruled India between approximately 320 AD and 550 AD.
  • This period is known as the 'Golden Age of India'.

questions.question: Badami was the earliest capital of the:
questions.solution:
Badami (Vatapi) was the earliest capital of the Chalukyas.
  • It is famous for its rock-cut temples.

questions.question: Which of the following Harappan sites is located in Afghanistan?
questions.solution:
Shortughai (and Mundigak) are the only major Harappan sites in Afghanistan.
  • They were important for Lapis Lazuli trade.

questions.question: Which of the following forts was built by the Kakatiya dynasty?
questions.solution:
Golconda Fort was originally a mud fort built by the Kakatiya Dynasty.
  • It later became the capital of the Qutub Shahi kings.

questions.question: In 1877, which of the following viceroys organised a durbar to acknowledge Queen Victoria as the Empress of India?
questions.solution:
Lord Lytton organized the Delhi Durbar of 1877.
  • Queen Victoria was proclaimed 'Kaiser-i-Hind' (Empress of India) at this event.

questions.question: Who among the following was the last ruler of Lodi dynasty of Delhi?
questions.solution:
Ibrahim Lodi was the last ruler of the Lodi Dynasty and the Delhi Sultanate.
  • He was the only Sultan to die on the battlefield.

questions.question: With reference to the early Indian history, who among the following was famous in the field of medicine?
questions.solution:
Charaka was the court physician of Kanishka and is known as the 'Father of Indian Medicine'.
  • He wrote the Charaka Samhita.

questions.question: Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq transferred his capital from Delhi to ______.
questions.solution:
Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (Devagiri) in 1327.
  • He is often called the 'Wise Fool' due to his ambitious but failed projects.

questions.question: The capital of the British Indian Empire was transferred from Calcutta to Delhi in:
questions.solution:
The capital of British India was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911.
  • This was announced during the Delhi Durbar of King George V.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the organisation ‘East India Association’?
questions.solution:
Dadabhai Naoroji, the 'Grand Old Man of India', founded the East India Association in London in 1866.
  • He was the first Indian to be a member of the British Parliament.

questions.question: Where did Lord Mahavira attain salvation?
questions.solution:
Lord Mahavira (the 24th Tirthankara) attained salvation (Nirvana) at Pawapuri (Bihar).
  • He was born at Kundagrama.

questions.question: The First Buddhist Council is said to have been patronised by:
questions.solution:
The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajgriha shortly after Buddha's death under the patronage of Ajatashatru.
  • It was presided over by Mahakashyapa.

questions.question: In which year was the Treaty of Versailles signed?
questions.solution:
The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919.
  • It formally ended World War I.

questions.question: Emperor Ashoka embraced Buddhism after the:
questions.solution:
Ashoka embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War (261 BC).
  • He replaced Bherighosha (war drum) with Dhammaghosha (sound of peace/Dharma).

questions.question: By which British statute were Indian representatives, for the first time, allocated seats for election in Indian Legislative Councils?
questions.solution:
The Indian Councils Act, 1892 introduced the principle of election (though indirect) for the first time.
  • It also gave members the right to discuss the budget.

questions.question: Which newspaper was founded by Mahatma Gandhi in South Africa in 1903?
questions.solution:
Indian Opinion was founded by Mahatma Gandhi in 1903 while he was in South Africa.
  • He also started Young India and Harijan in India.

questions.question: Which of the following associations/organisations was founded by Jyotiba Phule?
questions.solution:
Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (Truth Seekers' Society) in 1873.
  • He fought against the caste system and wrote the book 'Gulamgiri'.
